t: Section 306(a)(11)(D) of the Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act (7 U.S.C. 1926(a)(11)(D)) is amended by striking “1996 through 2007” and inserting “2008 through 2012”.

fable.w: This section only changes a date range in an existing statute, extending fiscal years from 1996-2007 to 2008-2012. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. The tempting reading is that the underlying rural development program may involve outside entities, but nothing in this text itself brings a non-federal party into a federal decision.

opus.w: The section is a technical amendment that changes a range of years in an existing provision. It does not involve any party outside the federal government in a federal decision. Any link to rural grant programs does not count, because grant applications are excluded from the definition of participation, and nothing in this text sets up a consultation or comment process.
opus.s: is amended by striking “1996 through 2007” and inserting “2008 through 2012”
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through:** Someone might be tempted to say "Yes" because the provision amends the Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act, which deals with grants and programs for rural communities. That reading fails. The amendment only swaps one range of fiscal years for another. It says nothing about consultation, hearings, comment periods, advisory bodies, rulemaking or a right to sue. And even if the underlying program involves grants, applying for a grant is not participation under the definition.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment that updates the effective dates of a provision in the Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act. It does not create any mechanism for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with non-federal entities. It simply changes the statutory time frame, which is an internal legislative action, not a participation process.
qwen_chat.s: Section 306(a)(11)(D) of the Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act (7 U.S.C. 1926(a)(11)(D)) is amended by striking “1996 through 2007” and inserting “2008 through 2012”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing the date range for a program could implicitly affect who participates in that program, or that the amendment itself is a "decision" involving outside parties. However, the text is purely a technical amendment to a statute's effective dates. It does not establish any process for consultation, comment, hearing, or advisory input from non-federal entities. It is a legislative change to the law's timeline, not a procedural requirement for participation in a federal decision-making process.
